🔊 Iran, Russia target 1,000 MW electricity exchange in new energy cooperation drive

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Iran and Russia have moved the project to connect their electricity grids via Azerbaijan into a new phase, setting a target of exchanging up to 1,000 megawatts of electricity after successful technical trials.

Mostafa Rajabi Mashhadi, Iran’s deputy energy minister for electricity and energy affairs, said on Tuesday that the project was discussed during talks between the energy ministers of Iran and Russia and is both technically and economically viable.
​
He said the electricity interconnection had already been tested successfully, adding that the first phase envisages the transfer of 300 MW before expanding to a capacity of 1,000 MW.
​
“We have previously verified the possibility of electricity exchange successfully during trial stages. We now plan, in the first phase, to operationalize the transfer of 300 megawatts and, in the development phase, up to 1,000 megawatts of electricity between the two countries,” Rajabi Mashhadi said.
​
He said the project would capitalize on the differing seasonal peak electricity demand in the two countries, with Iran’s demand peaking in summer and Russia’s in winter.
​
“Given the difference between the summer and winter peak consumption periods in the two countries, this exchange can be carried out as an energy swap or through rial-denominated buying and selling, which is highly attractive and economically justifiable for both sides,” he said.
